reasons.rpg3: Programs in RPG II / RPG III (RPG/400) need their processing flow worked out
reasons.source_missing: Some source code is missing and needs checking
reasons.source_vendor_held: The maintenance company or the vendor holds the source code, so you need to confirm they will hand it over
reasons.docs_outdated: Documents are outdated or missing, so the current specifications must be made visible first
reasons.integrations_many: Many interfaces make the switch-over more complex
reasons.acos_assembler: Parts written in assembler are hard to convert automatically or analyze with AI
reasons.access_vba: One-button processing (VBA, macros) means the business rules must be worked out
reasons.other_host: Mainframe and office computer assets tend to be large
reasons.small_scale: Size and customization look relatively small
reasons.support_passed: Support has already ended, which is a risk when something breaks
reasons.support_1_3y: Support ends in 1-3 years, so planned preparation is needed
reasons.maintenance_none: Nobody can change the system, neither in-house nor at a maintenance company
reasons.maintenance_retiring: The people who can change the system will retire or move within a few years
reasons.maintenance_few: Maintenance depends on one or two people
reasons.maintenance_vendor: Nobody in-house can change the system; it depends on a maintenance company
reasons.access_many_screens: Many screens and reports make the rebuild larger
reasons.access_many_tools: Many tools are in scope, so they need to be sorted out first
reasons.access_compiled: Some parts are compiled (.accde / .mde), so their behaviour must be investigated
reasons.access_single_maintainer: Only one person (or an outside individual) can change the tool
reasons.access_support_ended: Some of your Access (Office) versions are out of support
reasons.access_support_ending: Support for some of your Access (Office) versions ends within a year
reasons.access_company_impact: A stop would affect the whole company, partners or customers
reasons.access_cloud: Microsoft advises against using Access from OneDrive or SharePoint

result.checkpointsTitle: What to check when moving from {platform} to a web system
result.checkpointsTitleGeneric: What to check when moving to a web system

checkpoints.source_missing: First decide how to handle the missing source code (for example analyzing the running programs)
checkpoints.source_vendor_held: First confirm whether the maintenance company or the vendor will hand over the source code for the survey (contract and cost)
checkpoints.support_deadline: Plan a step-by-step migration that switches over before support ends
checkpoints.as400_tool: Write up the current specification from the design data of the development tool (Synon/2E, LANSA and so on)
checkpoints.as400_package: Separate the package from the changes made for your company, then decide how to move the changes and whether to update or replace the package
checkpoints.as400_version: Your IBM i version is out of IBM standard support: include the move to a supported environment in the migration plan
checkpoints.rpg3: Work out the processing flow of RPG II / RPG III (RPG/400) programs before migrating them
checkpoints.docs_outdated: Use AI to write the current specifications from the source code instead of the documents
checkpoints.integrations_many: Decide the switch-over order and data exchange for each interface
checkpoints.legacy_edi: Plan the switch of EDI over phone lines (INS Net) to an Internet-based method
checkpoints.as400_devices: Check printing on special forms and devices such as label printers and handheld terminals, and decide what replaces them on the Web
checkpoints.as400_query: List the data staff pull out with Query or Excel transfers and decide how they will get it after the migration
checkpoints.gaiji: Decide how to replace custom characters with Unicode
checkpoints.as400_screens: Replace the 5250 screens with Web screens while keeping the flow of operations
checkpoints.acos_assembler: Work out what the assembler parts do and rebuild them in a modern language
checkpoints.acos_charset: Convert the ACOS character codes (JIPS) and number formats (packed decimals and so on), and decide how to handle custom characters
checkpoints.acos_network_db: Design how to move the network database structure to a relational database
checkpoints.acos_simple_language: List the processing written in simple languages (IDL, IDL II) and rebuild it as Web features
checkpoints.acos_online: Replace the business screens used with ETOS and so on (MFDL screen definitions) with Web screens
checkpoints.acos_batch: Move the order and schedule of the overnight and month-end jobs (JCL) to the new system
checkpoints.access_no_maintainer: Investigate how the current tool behaves first, since nobody can change it
checkpoints.access_support: Move off an Office version that is out of support or about to be
checkpoints.access_vba: List the one-button processing (VBA, macros) and rebuild it as web features
checkpoints.access_size: Move to a database without the file size limit (about 2 GB)
checkpoints.access_excel: Keep Excel / CSV import and export as downloads and uploads on web screens
checkpoints.access_web: Make it a web system used in the browser, without the limits of shared files
checkpoints.other_vb: Separate Visual Basic screens and logic into web screens and server processing
checkpoints.other_webperformer: Check the WebPerformer screen definitions and logic to choose the approach
checkpoints.other_host: Take stock of COBOL and other programs, batch jobs and forms
checkpoints.other_inventory: First take stock of the current setup (languages, database, interfaces)
checkpoints.access_compiled: For compiled parts (.accde / .mde), check whether the originals exist and investigate the behaviour
checkpoints.access_inventory: First take stock of the tools and drop unused or duplicate ones to narrow the scope
checkpoints.access_cloud: Stop opening Access from cloud folders and move to a web system that shares data safely
checkpoints.access_external: Replace the links to data outside Access (core system, SQL Server) with web system interfaces
checkpoints.access_devices: Check how barcodes, label printers and other devices are used and decide their web replacements

difficultyText.low: Relatively small and simple. A closer look at the current system determines the outlook.
difficultyText.medium: A typical size. Clarify the current specification before choosing the migration approach.
difficultyText.high: Large or highly integrated. Start by making the specification visible and proceed in stages.

urgencyText.low: No immediate trouble, but planned preparation is recommended.
urgencyText.medium: Staffing or end of support will likely require a decision within a few years.
urgencyText.high: Business continuity risk is rising. We recommend assessing the current state soon.

people.title: People: a system that depends on a few individuals
people.problem: Years of changes have turned the specification into a black box, and fewer engineers can maintain it.
people.solution: Move to a web system the next generation can work with and remove the continuity risk.

cost.title: Cost: maintenance that limits growth
cost.problem: Rising maintenance costs leave little budget for growth initiatives.
cost.solution: Keep the initial investment low with a staged approach and shift budget to growth.

agility.title: Agility: a system that cannot keep up with the market
agility.problem: Every time you try to keep up with partners, markets or new ways of working, the limits of the current system or its support deadline hold you back.
agility.solution: Move to a supported Web platform that can take new features and use from outside the office right away.

data.title: Data: data that cannot support decisions
data.problem: Data is locked in proprietary formats, so management metrics are not available in real time.
data.solution: Use AI agents to organize data and get the information needed for proactive decisions.

noPrimaryChallenge.title: You see no major challenge at the moment

steps.title: Solve it with a step-by-step migration
steps.lead: No big-bang replacement. We start with a quick assessment and confirm the results at every step.

ax.title: AI transformation

targets.title: Systems we migrate
targets.lead: Not only core systems: business tools used by a single department are covered too.

as400.name: AS/400 (IBM i)
as400.body: Core systems written in RPG, COBOL or CL, moved to the web together with their screens, forms and data.

acos.name: NEC ACOS

access.name: Microsoft Access
access.body: Department Access tools brought together in a web system that many people can use safely.

other.name: Others
other.body: Visual Basic client-server systems, low-code products such as WebPerformer, and other office computers and mainframes.

keep.title: Migration that keeps the specifications

small.title: Start small

ax.title: Beyond the migration
ax.body: We continue on to AI agents and the use of your data.
